newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 1st half copper output to rise, zinc flat.
newsitem.headline: Japan 1st half copper output to rise, zinc flat.

text.p: Japan's eight non-ferrous metal refining companies plan to raise their total output of copper in the first half of 1997/98 from the year-ago period, semiannual production schedules released over the past week showed.
Copper output is forecast to rise 0.7 percent year-on-year to 642,006 tonnes in the six months ending September 30, while zinc output is seen little changed at 294,168 tonnes.
The higher refined copper output reflects a 5.4 percent rise in Sumitomo Metal Mining Co's production and a 3.4 percent rise at Nippon Mining and Metals Co.
Lead output is expected to decline 1.5 percent to 128,94 tonnes.

The eight companies are: Mitsubishi Materials Corp, Nippon Mining and Metals Co , Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co, Sumitomo Metal Mining Co, Furukawa Co, Dowa Mining Co, Toho Zinc Co and Nittetsu Mining Co.
